challenges.name: trace-context-quiz
challenges.title: Does this header continue the trace?
challenges.description: Headers captured between the CodeDev edge gateway, the API and grading-service on the day one submission showed up as three separate traces.

questions.explanation: True. W3C Trace Context defines trace-id and parent-id as lowercase hex (HEXDIGLC), and a receiver must ignore a traceparent whose ids contain anything else. The API's propagator did exactly that: it treated the request as having no parent and started a new trace. With lowercase ids the same header is valid, the API continues trace 4bf92f35... and its server span gets 00f067aa0ba902b7 as parent. Note the backend already shows the gateway's trace id in lowercase: it normalised it for display, which hides the problem in the UI. The misconception is that hex is hex: some parsers accept both cases, the spec does not, and a header that one hop accepts can be dropped by the next.

questions.question:
After the gateway fix, the API receives:
traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01

The API's server span for POST /submissions has span id 53995c3f42cd8ad8, and the HTTP client span for its call to grading-service has span id e457b5a2e4d86bd1. A reviewer proposes this for the outgoing call:

headers.traceparent = req.headers.traceparent; // forward as received

Statement: "Forwarding the header as received is correct: grading-service then sees parent-id 00f067aa0ba902b7 and its span appears under the API's call in the trace view."
questions.explanation: False. parent-id is the id of the caller's span, and each hop replaces it. The header the API sends must be 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-e457b5a2e4d86bd1-01: same trace-id, the API's client span as parent, sampled flag kept. Forwarding the gateway's header keeps the trace id, so the spans are still in one trace, but grading-service's span becomes a child of the gateway span 00f067aa0ba902b7, a sibling of the API's span: the tree no longer shows that grading ran inside the API's call, and the API's client span has no child. The misconception is that keeping the trace id is enough; the parent-id is what builds the tree, and an OpenTelemetry propagator writes it from the active span when you inject into the outgoing headers.

challenges.name: w3c-traceparent-propagation
challenges.title: Parse traceparent and continue the trace
challenges.description: The edge gateway in front of the CodeDev API wrote traceparent headers with upper-case ids, the API's tracer rejected them and started new traces, and the API then forwarded the header it had received to grading-service unchanged, so the trace view showed three disconnected pieces of one submission. Write the propagation code of the API's outgoing call to grading-service, following W3C Trace Context (https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/). parseTraceparent(header) returns { version, traceId, parentId, sampled } or null when the header is null or invalid. Trim spaces and tabs at both ends first. The header must be at least 55 characters; version is characters 0-1, two lowercase hex digits followed by "-", and "ff" is invalid. Version "00" must be exactly 55 characters: 00-<trace-id>-<parent-id>-<trace-flags>. A higher version (01 to fe) is parsed from its first 55 characters the same way, and when it is longer, character 55 must be "-" (the rest is not read). trace-id is 32, parent-id 16 and trace-flags 2 characters of lowercase hex (0-9, a-f only) with "-" between them; a trace-id or parent-id made only of zeros is invalid; sampled is the lowest bit of trace-flags (flags & 0x01). validTracestate(header) is true when the header is at most 512 characters and, split on "," with spaces and tabs trimmed around each member, has at least 1 and at most 32 non-empty members (empty members are allowed and ignored), no key twice, each member being key=value split at the first "=": key matches [a-z][a-z0-9_\-*/]{0,255} or [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_\-*/]{0,240}@[a-z][a-z0-9_\-*/]{0,13}, value is 1 to 256 characters from 0x20-0x7E except "," and "=" and does not end with a space. childHeaders(incoming, ids) returns { traceparent, tracestate } for the outgoing call. With a valid parent: "00-<same trace-id>-<new span id>-<flags>", where flags is "01" when sampled and "00" otherwise (always version 00, other flag bits set to 0), and tracestate is the exact string received when it is not null and valid, otherwise null. With a missing or invalid parent: a new trace, "00-<new trace id>-<new span id>-01", and tracestate null (never parse tracestate without a valid traceparent). New ids come from ids.traceId() (32 hex) and ids.spanId() (16 hex); an id made only of zeros must not be sent: draw again. Input (JSON on stdin): { traceIds, spanIds, requests: [{ traceparent?, tracestate? }] }; the id source returns the listed ids in turn. Output: a JSON array with, per request, { parent: parseTraceparent(traceparent), traceparent, tracestate } from childHeaders.
hints: A traceparent has fixed positions: where must the three dashes be for version 00, and what changes for a version you do not know yet? And of the four parts, which one does a service replace before it calls the next service?

Look at the order of your checks in parseTraceparent: trim, length, version (hex, not ff, then exact length for 00 or the character at index 55 for higher versions), then each field with a lowercase-only hex test (no i flag) and the all-zero test. In childHeaders the trace id stays, the span id is always new, and the flags are rebuilt from the sampled bit, not copied. tracestate is only looked at after the parent is valid.

Worked on other values: "00-11112222333344445555666677778888-aaaabbbbccccdddd-05" is valid (version 00, 55 characters) and 0x05 has the lowest bit set, so it is sampled; with a span id source returning "0000000000000000" then "1234567890abcdef", the outgoing header is "00-11112222333344445555666677778888-1234567890abcdef-01". "0a-11112222333344445555666677778888-aaaabbbbccccdddd-04+x" is invalid because character 55 is "+", while the same header ending in "-04-x" is accepted with sampled false. A tracestate of "acme=1,ACME=2" is dropped (upper-case key).

tests.name: Valid parents keep trace id and sampled flag; a missing header starts a new trace
The incident: upper-case ids, all-zero ids and version ff are rejected
Higher versions: parse the first 55 characters and answer with version 00
Version 00 is exactly 55 characters; spaces and tabs around it are trimmed
Trace flags: only the sampled bit is kept, other bits are set to 0
tracestate passes unchanged only when it is valid and the parent is valid
An all-zero id from the id source is never sent: draw again
Large: 360 requests from gateways, browsers and old SDKs
